chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

text.first-impression: Okay, Gap. Here's what people clock in the first ten seconds: confidence, opinions, and posture like you're about to give a talk nobody booked. You walk in like the room should rearrange itself around you. Half the time it does, which is annoying for everyone else and great for you. People assume you're in charge, so they hand you things: projects, problems, the restaurant booking. You take them, obviously. What they don't see right away is that you're quite sensitive about being respected. You'd rather be right than liked. You'd prefer both. And you get grumpy when you can only pick one. That's the read. You're welcome.
text.your-red-flag: Your red flag? You don't bend. At all. A tree grows straight up, and you've decided that's a personality trait instead of a botanical fact. You'll listen to feedback, nod thoughtfully, and then do exactly what you'd already planned. You call it conviction. Everyone else calls it the reason they say can someone else talk to Gap. Being stubborn about values is admirable. Being stubborn about which route to the cinema is just tiring for the people in the car. Bom says you're principled. I say you're principled about things that are not principles. Learn the difference and you'll be unstoppable instead of merely unmovable.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you lead. You plan the dates, the trips, the five-year outline nobody asked to see. Partners love it at first, then quietly realize they're passengers in their own relationship. Your sabotage move is deciding what the relationship is and then being genuinely confused when the other person has opinions about it. You also pick people who need you, because being needed feels like being loved, and then resent carrying them. That's a loop, and you built it. Try someone who wants to walk beside you, not behind you. And when they disagree, say tell me more before you start drafting your rebuttal. Revolutionary, I know.
text.friends-and-work: At work you end up leading even when nobody hired you to. Great for your career, slightly terrifying for your coworkers, who have learned to just agree in meetings. You're fair, driven, and convinced that I'll just do it myself is a strategy. It's not. It's a burnout plan with good branding. With friends you're loyal to the bone. You'll show up for the move, the breakup, the crisis at 1am. But you give advice like you're billing by the hour. Sometimes your friends don't want a five-point plan. They want you to say that sucks. Two words. You can manage two words.
text.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm fine, I just have a lot going on. You always have a lot going on, because you keep adding things to the pile and calling it ambition. You treat rest like a reward you haven't quite earned yet. You also tell yourself you don't need anyone's approval, which is adorable, because you absolutely want respect from the people you respect. That's not weakness, Gap. It's being a person. Admit it, out loud if you're brave, and you'll stop overworking to earn something the people who matter are already giving you.
text.the-fix: Fine. Bom made me add a fix chapter, so here it is. Bend a little, on purpose, on small things. Let someone else pick the restaurant and don't comment on the menu. Ask one question a day that you don't already know the answer to. Rest before you're empty, not after you've collapsed. In love, choose someone strong enough to tell you no, and then actually let them win sometimes. You're a tall tree. You give shade, structure and direction to a lot of people. You'll be even better when you stop treating flexibility like an attack. Okay. I'm done being nice. That was a lot for me.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap. Gap enters a party like it's a board meeting.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It's called refusing to let anyone else pick the restaurant.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Bend once, Gap. Trees that never bend snap. Trees can sway, you know.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: But Gap is so loyal and fair!

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. Now say 'tell me more' before the rebuttal. Practice.

spring.intro: Spring Gap Wood, let's be honest. You were born when Wood ran the whole season, so you got a double helping of yourself: upright, principled and absolutely convinced you're right. People clock it in ten seconds. You stand like the podium is already yours. Your red flag is treating disagreement like a structural threat. Someone suggests another restaurant and you defend your choice like it's a load-bearing wall. Your friends love that you're reliable. They also have a group chat where they decide things before telling you. The fix is boring and effective: lose one argument a week on purpose and watch nothing collapse.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You defended your restaurant choice like a thesis. It was a sandwich place.

summer.intro: Summer Gap, you arrived when Fire ran things, and Wood exists to feed Fire. Translation: you're a giver who can't stop giving opinions, plans, help and unsolicited life advice. You show love by volunteering for everything. The red flag is that you burn yourself out and then quietly resent everyone for letting you. Nobody asked you to organize the group holiday, plan the birthday and fix your friend's résumé in one week. You offered. Then you sighed loudly about it. Bom says you're generous. You are. You're also a martyr with a calendar. Stop offering things you don't want to do, and the resentment has nothing to eat.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You volunteered for three things, then sighed about all three. Pick one, Gap.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gap, your season belonged to Metal and Metal is the axe to your tree. So you grew up with a strict inner critic and turned it into a personality. You judge yourself hard and, surprise, you judge everyone else by the same rulebook. People notice the raised eyebrow before you say a word. Your red flag is calling it having standards when sometimes it's just being harsh. In love you prune people: one mistake and they're off the shortlist. At work you're the person who corrects the slide deck during the meeting. The fix: before you judge, ask one curious question. Shocking how often it changes the verdict.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You corrected a typo in someone's birthday message. In the group chat. Publicly.

winter.intro: Winter-born Gap: Water ran the season and Water feeds Wood, so you've got deep roots and the patience of a glacier. Nice. Also: you overthink everything and call it being thorough. People see a calm, solid person. Your friends know you need three business days to reply to pizza or Thai. Your red flag is stubborn stillness: you won't move until you're absolutely certain, and you're rarely absolutely certain. In love you wait for perfect conditions that don't exist. At work you research a decision until it's out of date. The fix is a rule: small choices get five minutes. Roots are great. Trees still have to grow.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pizza or Thai should not require a pros and cons list, Gap.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Gap, the end-of-season weeks when the ground takes over. Wood controls Earth, so you grew up managing terrain: chores, plans, other people's half-finished ideas. People see a capable leader. Your friends see someone who turns a picnic into a project. Your red flag is treating people like ground to be organized. In love, partners feel scheduled. At work, you volunteer for everything and resent it quietly by Thursday. The fix: let one thing stay messy this week and don't touch it. The field survives.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Not everything is a project, Gap. Some things are just Tuesday.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Gap. Lots of Wood and Water backing you up, which explains the confidence and the inability to say fair point. You're not arrogant exactly. You're just sure, all the time, about everything. The blind spot: you steamroll. People stop disagreeing with you, not because you're right but because it's tiring. Your friends defer. Your partner stops bringing things up. You think that's harmony. It's surrender. The fix: in your next disagreement, say tell me more and mean it. Being a big tree is great. Blocking everyone's sun is not.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Gap, meaning not much in your corner, so you've built that upright posture by pure effort. Respect. But here's the thing: you overcompensate. You say yes to prove you're capable, take on too much to prove you're useful, then crash quietly. The blind spot is shrinking in plain sight while looking tall. You give way in arguments you were winning because you doubt yourself. You let people take the credit. The fix: next time you're right, stay right. Out loud. Stop apologizing for taking up space. Trees are supposed to.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything feels urgent, out loud or only on the inside, and your feelings arrive with sirens on even when nobody else can hear them. You're bright company, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the color, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyze it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair color twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
